visual: Dense, compact deciduous shrub with dark green palmately lobed leaves, flat heads of small fertile flowers surrounded by creamy-white sterile flowers, followed by bright red berries.
soil: Chalk, clay, loam or sand; acid, neutral or alkaline
soilWarning: Avoid very dry or persistently waterlogged soil. Moist, humus-rich ground produces the strongest growth and fruiting.
prune: Pruning group 1; prune after flowering if required, but avoid heavy pruning if the ornamental berries are wanted.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten; wear gloves and appropriate protection when handling.
hardinessNote: Hardy throughout the UK and northern Europe; RHS rates it H6.
resilience: Robust and adaptable shrub that tolerates exposed positions and a range of soils when moisture is adequate.
uses: Shrub borders, woodland gardens, cottage gardens, wildlife gardens, hedging, informal screening and specimen planting.
foliage: Deciduous; dark green, palmately lobed leaves turning purplish-red in autumn.
container: Possible in a large container, although it performs best planted in the ground.
